title: Party treasure pool and item claims
summary: The DM can put loot in the party's treasure pool, players claim Need, Greed or Pass, and the DM hands items out fairly in one step.
items: Party → Treasure pool lists the items waiting for the party. Each player marks Need, Greed or Pass for their characters; claims are visible to the whole party and never move anything.
The DM puts items in the pool from Add loot (when the owner is a party fund) or from an encounter's loot review with Treasure pool as the recipient or Send all items to the treasure pool.
Review Inbox → Treasure pool claims resolves items one at a time, at random (Need first, then Greed, with d100 rolls or Pen & Paper totals) or round-robin, with a preview before anything moves.
Every item moves once, even after a lost connection: if a claim changes during review, nothing moves and the DM reviews again.
Pooled items stay in the party fund but can't be given, sold, offered or equipped until the DM resolves them or takes them out of the pool.
Each resolution appears once in Activity and the party chat, and the pool's History tab shows who received what, with any rolls.
Claims can be sent outside a player's turn. Players away from the party see only their own claims and items, and items given to companion NPCs stay private to the DM.
